draft.title: The behavioural approach
card: The behavioural approach says that people are not machines. How workers feel about their job and their team affects how well they work.
Elton Mayo ran the Hawthorne studies at a factory in the United States in the 1920s and 1930s. Output rose when workers were given attention, even when conditions did not improve.
The studies suggested that attention, teamwork and meeting social needs, such as belonging and respect, can lift motivation. Pay is not the only thing that motivates people.
Managers using this approach lead and consult rather than only give orders. They listen to workers, build teams and take an interest in them.
draft.remember: Motivation can grow when workers feel noticed, valued and part of a team.

a.q: Which action by a manager best fits the behavioural approach?
opts: Holding regular team meetings to ask staff for ideas
Timing each task so workers can be paid per item
Writing a rule book that sets every worker's duties
Cutting staff to lower the wage bill
a.why: Asking staff for ideas shows consultation and meets social needs, which the behavioural approach says can lift motivation. Paying per item is tempting, but it relies on pay alone and treats workers as parts of a machine.
a.clue: Which action treats workers as people with social needs?

b.q: Priya manages a call centre in Parramatta. Sales are flat. She stops checking call times, starts weekly team lunches and asks staff how to improve the work. Sales rise. Which idea best explains this?
opts: Attention and teamwork can lift motivation
Close timing of tasks always raises output
A strict chain of command keeps order
Workers only respond to higher pay
b.why: Priya gave attention, built teamwork and consulted staff, and output rose. This matches Mayo's findings that social needs can lift motivation. Timing tasks is a different approach, and nothing here involved a change in pay.
b.clue: Look at what Priya changed, and what she did not change.

a.best: Holding regular team meetings to ask staff for ideas

b.best: Attention and teamwork can lift motivation

problems.detail: 'Elton Mayo ran the Hawthorne studies' overstates his role. Western Electric and the National Research Council began the studies at the Hawthorne Works near Chicago in 1924. Mayo joined around 1927–28 and led the later phases with Roethlisberger and Dickson. Safer wording is 'Elton Mayo led the best-known Hawthorne studies' or 'Elton Mayo is linked to the Hawthorne studies'.

Two distractors use absolute words ('Workers only respond to higher pay', 'Close timing of tasks always raises output'), while the card uses 'can'. These words make the distractors easy to rule out without knowing the idea.
